3. Crl.P.No.3398/2021 is filed by the petitioners- accused Nos.1 to 5 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.56926/2019 arising out of Crime No.475/2018 registered by H.A.L. Police Station, Bengaluru and charge-sheet for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 324 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the D.P. Act, pending on the file of 43rd Additional CMM, Bengaluru.
4.

Crl.P.No.1490/2023 is filed by the petitioners- accused Nos.1 to 4 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.17447/2020 arising out of Crime No.183/2019 registered by H.A.L. Police Station, Bengaluru and charge-sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504, 506, 420, 406, 120B, 379, 389 read with Section 34 of IPC, pending on the file of IV Additional CMM, Bengaluru.

5. During pendency of the petition, both petitioners and respondents have filed joint compromise applications on I.A.Nos.1/2023 under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. along with affidavit in both the cases seeking permission of this Court to compound the offences and it is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent that petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 in both the cases are husband and wife vice versa and due to family dispute, there was a case and counter case registered against each persons and charge-sheeted by the Police.
Now both of them have compromised between them in the matrimonial case and they have decided to reside together and lead happy marital life.
Accused Nos.2 to 5 and accused Nos.2 to 4 in both the cases are the parents of both the parties.

In view of the settlement between the parties, as they have decided to lead happy marital life and they have dissolved all the dispute between them amicably in the interest of their family affairs and future family life, the interlocutory applications filed by the petitioners and respondent shall have to be allowed and permitted the parties to compound the offences.
6. Accordingly, both the applications are allowed.
Consequently, criminal petitions are allowed.
